questions.q: A ball of mass $10kg$ moving with a velocity $10\sqrt{3}m{s}^{- 1}$ along the $x$ -axis, hits another ball of mass $20kg$ which is at rest. After the collision, first ball comes to rest while the second ball disintegrates into two equal pieces. One piece starts moving along $y$ -axis with a speed of $10m{s}^{- 1} .$ The second piece starts moving at an angle of $30 °$ with respect to the $x$ -axis. The velocity of the ball moving at $30 °$ with $x$ -axis is $xm{s}^{- 1} .$ The configuration of pieces after the collision is shown in the figure below. The value of $x$ to the nearest integer is
questions.solution:
Let the velocity of ${2}^{\text{nd}}$ fragment is $\overset{\to}{v}$ then by conservation of linear momentum
$10 ( 10\sqrt{3} ) \overset{^}{i} = ( 10 ) ( 10\overset{^}{j} ) + 10\overset{\to}{v}$
$⇒ \overset{\to}{v} = 10\sqrt{3}\overset{^}{i} - 10\overset{^}{j}$
$| \overset{\to}{v} | = \sqrt{300 + 100} = \sqrt{400} = 20m{s}^{- 1}$.

questions.q: Four forces are acting at a point $P$ in equilibrium as shown in figure. The ratio of force ${F}_{1}$ to ${F}_{2}$ is $1: x$ where $x =$_____ .
questions.solution:
Here, $\theta = 45 °$

Applying equilibrium conditions,

Taking components along $x$ & $y$

Considering right side positive, $∑ {F}_{x} = 0$

${F}_{1} + 1sin45 ° - 2sin45 ° = 0{F}_{1} = 2sin45 ° - 1sin45 °$

${F}_{1} = \sqrt{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{2 - 1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Taking upward positive,$∑ {F}_{y} = 0$

$1cos45 ° + 2cos45 ° - {F}_{2} = 0{F}_{2} = 1cos45 ° + 2cos45 °$

${F}_{2} = \sqrt{2} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{2 + 1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$

${F}_{1}: {F}_{2} = 1: 3$

$x = 3$

questions.q: A nucleus disintegrates into two nuclear parts, in such a way that ratio of their nuclear sizes is $1: {2}^{1 / 3}$. Their respective speed have a ratio of $n: 1$. The value of $n$ is_________
questions.solution:
Using the law of Momentum conservation

${m}_{1}{v}_{1} + {m}_{2} ( - {v}_{2} ) = 0$
$⇒ {m}_{1}{v}_{1} = {m}_{2}{v}_{2}$
$⇒ \left(\dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}}\right) = \left(\dfrac{{v}_{2}}{{v}_{1}}\right) ⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{4\piρ{r}^{3}1}{3}}{\dfrac{4\piρ{r}^{3}2}{3}} = \left(\dfrac{{v}_{2}}{{v}_{1}}\right)$

It is given

$\dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{{2}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}$
$\text{and}{\left(\dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}}\right)}^{3} = \left(\dfrac{{v}_{2}}{{v}_{1}}\right)\text{Therefore}, \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{{v}_{2}}{{v}_{1}}\right)$
$⇒ \dfrac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

questions.q:
If one wants to remove all the mass of the earth to infinity in order to break it up completely. The amount of energy that needs to be supplied will be $\dfrac{x}{5}\dfrac{G{M}^{2}}{R}$ where $x$ is ________.

(Round off to the Nearest Integer)

($M$ is the mass of earth, $R$ is the radius of earth, $G$ is the gravitational constant)
questions.solution:
Energy given $= {U}_{f} - {U}_{i}$

$= 0 - \left(- \dfrac{3}{5}\dfrac{G{M}^{2}}{R}\right)$

$= \dfrac{3}{5}\dfrac{G{M}^{2}}{R}$

$x = 3$

questions.q: A system to $10$ balls each of mass $2kg$ are connected via massless and unstretchable string. The system is allowed to slip over the edge of a smooth table as shown in figure. Tension on the string between the ${7}^{th}$ and ${8}^{th}$ ball is _____ $N$ when ${6}^{th}$ ball just leaves the table.
questions.solution:
Acceleration,$a = \dfrac{Netpullingforce}{Totalmass}$

$a = \dfrac{6mg}{10m} = \dfrac{6g}{10} = 6m{s}^{- 2}$

Considering ball $8, 9 \text{ and } 10$ as system, tension between ball 7 & 8 can be written as,

${T}_{7, 8} = \left(3m\right) \times a$

$= 3 \times 2 \times 6 = 36N$

questions.q:
Three students ${S}_{1}, {S}_{2}$ and ${S}_{3}$ perform an experiment for determining the acceleration due to gravity $( g )$ using a simple pendulum. They use different lengths of pendulum and record time for different number of oscillations. The observations are as shown in the table.

Student No. Length of pendulum
$( cm )$		 Number of oscillations
$( n )$		 Total time for
$n$ oscillations		 Time
period
$( s )$
$1 .$ $64 . 0$ $8$ $128 . 0$ $16 . 0$
$2 .$ $64 . 0$ $4$ $64 . 0$ $16 . 0$
$3 .$ $20 . 0$ $4$ $36 . 0$ $9 . 0$

(Least count of length $= 0 . 1m$, least count for time $= 0 . 1s$)

If ${E}_{1}, {E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{3}$ are the percentage errors in $g$ for students $1, 2$ and $3$, respectively, then the minimum percentage error is obtained by student no .
questions.solution:
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{ℓ}{g}} ⇒ g = \dfrac{4{\pi}^{2}ℓ}{{T}^{2}}$
$\dfrac{\Deltag}{g} = \dfrac{\Deltaℓ}{ℓ} + \dfrac{2 ∆ T}{T}$

$\DeltaT = \dfrac{leastcountoftime\left(\Delta{T}_{0}\right)}{numberofoscillations ( n )}$
$\dfrac{\Deltag}{g} = \dfrac{\Deltaℓ}{ℓ} + \dfrac{2\Delta{T}_{0}}{nT}$

As $\Deltaℓ$ and $\Delta{T}_{0}$ are same for all observations so
$\dfrac{\Deltag}{g}$ is minimum for highest value of $ℓ, n$ and $T$

$⇒$ Minimum percentage error in $g$ is for student number 1.

questions.q: The length of a metallic wire is increased by $20 %$ and its area of cross-section is reduced by $4 % .$ The percentage change in resistance of the metallic wire is $________ .$
questions.solution:
The given data is

$l ' = 1 . 2lA ' = 0 . 96A$

Using the formula $R = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$, the new resistance is

${R}^{'} = \dfrac{1 . 2ρl}{0 . 96A}$

$⇒ {R}^{'} = 1 . 25R$

$⇒ \DeltaR = 1 . 25R - R = 0 . 25R$

Hence, the percentage increase is

$= \dfrac{\DeltaR}{R} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 25R}{R} \times 100 = 25 %$

questions.q: A particle is moving with constant acceleration $a .$ Following graph shows ${v}^{2}$ versus $x$ (displacement) plot. The acceleration of the particle is _________ $m{s}^{- 2} .$
questions.solution:
The equation of the straight line, $y = mx + c$, from the above graph we get the equation, ${v}^{2} = 2x + 20$, now differentiate it with respect to $x$,
$⇒ 2v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 2 ⇒ a = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1m{s}^{- 2}$.

questions.q: From the top of a tower, a ball is thrown vertically upward which reaches the ground in $6s$. A second ball thrown vertically downward from the same position with the same speed reaches the ground in $1 . 5s$. A third ball released, from the rest from the same location, will reach the ground in _____ s.
questions.solution:
When it is thrown upward, $- h = v \times 6 - \dfrac{1}{2}g{\left(6\right)}^{2}$

When it is thrown downward, $- h = - v \times 1 . 5 - \dfrac{1}{2}g{\left(1 . 5\right)}^{2}$

Therefore, $5h = 5\left[36 + 9\right]$ $h = 45m$

When the ball is dropped, $h = \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}^{2} ⇒ 45 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times {t}^{2} ⇒ t = 3s$

Alternate method, $t = \sqrt{{t}_{1}{t}_{2}} = \sqrt{6 \times 1 . 5} = 3s$

questions.q: For a train engine moving with speed of $20{ms}^{– 1}$, the driver must apply brakes at a distance of $500m$ before the station for the train to come to rest at the station. If the brakes were applied at half of this distance, the train engine would cross the station with speed $\sqrt{x}{ms}^{- 1}$. The value of $x$ is ______. (Assuming same retardation is produced by brakes)
questions.solution:
Given that, the initial velocity $u = 20m / s$, the distance of the station ${S}_{1} = 500m$, and the final velocity $v = 0$.

The relation between the distance travelled $\left(S\right)$ by the train with its initial velocity $\left(u\right)$ and its final velocity $\left(v\right)$ is given by

${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} - 2aS . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where, $a$ indicates the retardation of the train.

Substitute the values corresponding to the initial condition into equation (1) and solve to calculate the retardation of the train.

$\begin{cases}0 & = & ( 20{)}^{2} - 2 \times a \times 500 \\ a & = & 0 . 4m / {s}^{2}\end{cases}$

For the second scenario, the initial velocity $u = 20m / s$ and the distance travelled by the train ${S}_{2} = 250m$.

Use these values along with the value of the retardation into equation (1) and solve to calculate the final velocity of the train.

$\begin{cases}{v}^{2} & = & ( 20{)}^{2} - 2 \times 0 . 4 \times 250 \\ & = & 200 \\ v & = & \sqrt{200} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 2 )\end{cases}$

Comparing the value of the final velocity obtained in equation (2) with the given expression, we get $x = 200$.

questions.q: A particle of mass $10g$moves in a straight line with retardation $2x,$ where $x$ is the displacement in $SI$ units. Its loss of kinetic energy for above displacement is ${\left(\dfrac{10}{x}\right)}^{- n}J .$ The value of $n$ will be $________ .$
questions.solution:
Acceleration can be written as, $a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx}$.

Given: $a = - 2x$(-ve sign is due to retardation)

Therefore,

$v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = - 2x ⇒ vdv = \left(- 2x\right)dx$

Integrating both sides, we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left({v}_{f}^{2} - {v}_{i}^{2}\right) = - 2\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right) = {x}^{2} ⇒ \left|\dfrac{1}{2}m\left({v}_{f}^{2} - {v}_{i}^{2}\right)\right| = m{x}^{2}$

$⇒ | \DeltaKE | = 0 . 01{x}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{10}{x}\right)}^{- 2}$

Hence, $n = 2$.

questions.q: A swimmer wants to cross a river from point $A$ to point $B$. Line AB makes an angle of $30 °$ with the flow of the river. The magnitude of the velocity of the swimmer is the same as that of the river. The angle $\theta$ with the line $AB$ should be _______$°$, so that the swimmer reaches point $B$.
questions.solution: Both velocity vectors are of same magnitude therefore resultant would pass exactly midway through them $\theta = 30 °$

questions.q:
If the initial velocity in horizontal direction of a projectile is unit vector $\overset{^}{i}$ and the equation of trajectory is $y = 5x\left(1 - x\right)$. The $y$ component vector of the initial velocity is _____ $\overset{^}{j}$

(Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Given here, initial velocity, ${u}_{x} = 1$

Equation of trajectory, $y = 5x\left(1 - x\right) = 5x - 5{x}^{2}$

Now, differentiating the above equation,

$\dfrac{d y}{d t} = 5\dfrac{d x}{d t} - 10x\dfrac{d x}{d t}$

For initial $y$-component of velocity

${u}_{y} = {\left(\dfrac{d y}{d t}\right)}_{x = 0} ⇒ 5\left(1\right) = 5$

$\overset{\to}{u}y = 5\overset{^}{j}$

questions.q: An object is projected in the air with initial velocity $u$ at an angle $\theta$. The projectile motion is such that the horizontal range $R$, is maximum. Another object is projected in the air with a horizontal range half of the range of first object. The initial velocity remains same in both the case. The value of the angle of projection, at which the second object is projected, will be _____  degree.
questions.solution:
The maximum range is given by, ${R}_{max} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}sin2\left(45 °\right)}{g} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}}{g}$.

For the range to be half of the maximum range,

$\dfrac{{R}_{max}}{2} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}}{2g} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}sin2\theta}{g}$

$⇒ sin2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 2\theta = 30 ° \text{or}2\theta = 150 °$

$⇒ \theta = 15 ° , 75 °$

Therefore, answer is $15\text{or}75$

questions.q: A force $\overset{\to}{F} = ( \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} ) N$ acts at a point $( 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} ) m$. Then the magnitude of torque about the point $( \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) m$ will be $\sqrt{x}N - m .$The value of $x$ is..........
questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{r} = \left(4 - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(- 1 - 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$= 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

$τ = \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{F} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & j & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 1 & - 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i}\left(7\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(11\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(5\right) = 7\overset{^}{i} - 11\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

$= \sqrt{49 + 121 + 25} = \sqrt{195}$

questions.q:
Moment of Inertia (M.I.) of four bodies having same mass $M$ and radius $2R$ are as follows
${I}_{1} =$ M.I. of solid sphere about its diameter
${I}_{2} =$ M.I. of solid cylinder about its axis
${I}_{3} =$ M.I. of solid circular disc about its diameter
${I}_{4} =$ M.I. of thin circular ring about its diameter
If $2\left({I}_{2} + {I}_{3}\right) + {I}_{4} = x{I}_{1}$ then the value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.solution:
$∵ 2\left({I}_{2} + {I}_{3}\right) + {I}_{4} = x{I}_{1}$

Now

For solid sphere about its diameter ${I}_{1} = \dfrac{2}{5}M{R}^{2}$,

For solid cylinder about its axis ${I}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}M{R}^{2}$,

For circular disc about its diameter ${I}_{3} = \dfrac{1}{4}M{R}^{2}$

And for circular ring about its diameter ${I}_{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}M{R}^{2}$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{4}\right) + \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2} = x \times \dfrac{2}{5}M{R}^{2}$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2} = x \times \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ 2 = x \times \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ x = 5$

questions.q: A solid cylinder is released from rest from the top of an inclined plane of inclination $30 °$ and length $60cm$. If the cylinder rolls without slipping, its speed upon reaching the bottom of the inclined plane is ______ $m{s}^{- 1}$. (Given $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Let speed of cylinder upon reaching the bottom of the inclined plane be $v$.

Here, gain in kinetic energy$=$loss in potential energy

So, $\dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = mglsin\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{m{r}^{2}}{2}\right){\omega}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = mglsin30 °$

For pure rolling, $v = r\omega$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{m{r}^{2}}{2}\right){\left(\dfrac{v}{r}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = mglsin30 °$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = mglsin30 ° ⇒ \dfrac{3}{4}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{mgl}{2} ⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{4gl}{6}}$

Putting the values, we have

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{4 \times 10 \times 0 . 6}{6}} = 2m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: The potential energy $\left(U\right)$ of a diatomic molecule is a function dependent on $r$ (interatomic distance) as $U = \dfrac{\alpha}{{r}^{10}} - \dfrac{\beta}{{r}^{5}} - 3$ where, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are positive constants. The equilibrium distance between two atoms will be $\left(\dfrac{2\alpha}{\beta}\right)\dfrac{a}{b},$ where $a =$______ .
questions.solution:
For equilibrium

$\dfrac{dU}{dr} = 0$

$\dfrac{- 10\alpha}{{r}^{11}} + \dfrac{5\beta}{{r}^{6}} = 0$

$\dfrac{5\beta}{{r}^{6}} = \dfrac{10\alpha}{{r}^{11}}$

${r}^{5} = \dfrac{2\alpha}{\beta}$

${r}^{5} = \dfrac{2\alpha}{\beta}$

$r = \left(\dfrac{2\alpha}{\beta}\right)\dfrac{1}{5}a = 1$

questions.q:
A ball of mass $100g$ is dropped from a height $h = 10cm$ on a platform fixed at the top of a vertical spring (as shown in figure). The ball stays on the platform and the platform is depressed by a distance $\dfrac{h}{2}$. The spring constant is _____ $N{m}^{- 1}$
(Use $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Loss in the gravitational potential energy of the ball= gain in the potential energy by the spring

$- ∆ P{E}_{gravitational} = ∆ P{E}_{spring}$

$mg\left(h + \dfrac{h}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}k{\left(\dfrac{h}{2}\right)}^{2}$$⇒$$mg\dfrac{3h}{2} = \dfrac{k{h}^{2}}{8}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{12mg}{h} = \dfrac{12 \times 0 . 1 \times 10}{0 . 1} = 120N{m}^{- 1}$

questions.q: A block of mass '$m$' (as shown in figure) moving with kinetic energy $E$ compresses a spring through a distance $25cm$ when, its speed is halved. The value of spring constant of used spring will be $nEN{m}^{- 1}$ for $n =$_____.
questions.solution:
Using work $-$ energy theorem

${W}_{net} = ∆ KE$

${W}_{net} = \left({K}_{f} - {K}_{i}\right)$

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2}K{x}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} ⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2}K{x}^{2} = \dfrac{E}{4} - E$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}K{x}^{2} = \dfrac{3E}{4} ⇒ K = \dfrac{3E}{2{x}^{2}}$

$⇒ K = \dfrac{3E}{2 \times {\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}} = 24EN{m}^{- 1}$

Thus, the value of $n = 24$.

questions.q:
A uniform disc with mass $M = 4kg$ and radius $R = 10cm$ is mounted on a fixed horizontal axle as shown in figure. A block with mass $m = 2kg$ hangs from a massless cord that is wrapped around the rim of the disc. During the fall of the block, the cord does not slip and there is no friction at the axle. The tension in the cord is _____ $N$.

(Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Let $a$ be the acceleration of block and $\alpha$ be the angular acceleration of disc.

Now, for unwrapping without slipping, $R\alpha = a$.

Forces acting on block are shown in FDB.

Using Newton's second law

$mg - T = ma . . . \left(1\right)$

Torque about centre of disc is $τ = Ia$

$TR = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2}\alpha = \dfrac{4{R}^{2}}{2}\alpha = ⇒ T = 2R\alpha . . . \left(2\right)$

Putting the value of tension in equation $\left(1\right)$, we get

$mg - 2R\alpha = ma ⇒ mg - 2R\dfrac{a}{R} = ma ⇒ mg - 2a = ma ⇒ ma + 2a = mg ⇒ a = \dfrac{mg}{m + 2} = \dfrac{2 \times 10}{2 + 2} = 5m{s}^{- 2}$

Now, $\alpha = \dfrac{5}{0 . 1} = 50rad{s}^{- 2}$

Tension in the cord is $T = 2 \times 0 . 1 \times 50 =$$10N$.
